title: Auto Mode Becomes Default for Pro, Max, and Team Plans
description: Starting August 14, 2026, Claude Code made auto mode the default permission mode for new sessions on Pro, Max, and Team plans. Anthropic reports auto mode's AI safety review caught 89% of dangerous commands while humans only caught 13.6%. Users approved 97% of permission prompts habitually, making manual review mostly a formality.

community_feedback.quote: Their newer models are heavily trained out of the 'whoopsie doopsie I deleted prod' behaviour from last year. It's extremely anal about standard 'hygiene' stuff like not leaving plaintext secrets lying around. More sensible, and more cybersecurity-minded than the bottom 80% of IT professionals.
Claude Code ended up running a test that ran `rm -rf` on his home directory.
Auto Mode has mostly made me more productive but expressed frustration with content filters interfering with work, leading them to downgrade and try Chinese models like Kimi & Qwen.
Auto mode will also happily do stuff like write into your user's SSH config and leave you with permanently broken SSH.
If you go full auto, there will be collateral damage. Users trust Claude Code because it asks before doing anything.
As of today, that classifier overhead no longer counts toward your usage limits on Pro, Max, and Team plans.
Claude found their personal financial ledger elsewhere on their hard drive when working on nonprofit books, calling it 'a bit of an overreach.'

title: Session-to-Session Messaging
description: Claude Code sessions can now message each other using the ListAgents tool and SendMessage. Claude can communicate between sessions without re-explaining context when a change in one session affects what another is working on. Available on macOS and Linux, requires v2.1.224 or later.

title: Self-Hosted Environments (Public Beta)
description: Team and Enterprise plans can now run Claude Code cloud sessions on their organization's own infrastructure. Run `claude self-hosted-runner` on machines or containers to turn them into runners. Sessions run inside your network with access to internal services.

title: Weekly Limits Promotion Extended Through August 31
description: Claude Code extended its 50% higher weekly limits promotion through August 31, 2026 for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise users. Originally set to end August 19, the extension comes as users reported frustration with rapid usage depletion and outages.

community_feedback.quote: Between the outages and just overall crap utility of Opus/Fable lately, I was considering canceling my subscription.
With ultracode active, multiple agents ate my $100 credit in no time flat while producing nothing useful.
I made the full switch to 5.6 sol and Codex about a month ago. Better experience, higher limits and better output than Opus 4.8. Almost 0 switching cost - just rename your Claude.md to agents.md.
OpenAI weekly limits feel infinite compared to Anthropic's.
I'm 100% convinced that its verbose writing style is to generate tokens to make you hit your limit quicker.
Anthropic has been struggling all of 2026 with usage limits and shenanigans around 'peak hour' reduction.
The race is actually between locally optimized rigs with extremely strict context management, and the rest.

title: Skill and Plugin Security Scanning (Beta)
description: Enterprise plans can now enable automatic security scanning for third-party skills and plugins when uploaded or edited. Helps detect malicious content before deployment.

title: Origin Code Hosting Platform Launch
description: Cursor launched Origin, a new Git hosting platform in early beta for paid plans. Features include hosted codebases with GitHub repo syncing, pull requests with two-way sync, agent integration for code analysis, and app extensions for Vercel, Depot, and Buildkite. Launch coincided with GitHub's 7-hour outage on August 17.

community_feedback.quote: It's like going from bad to worse.
They are doing the easiest part of git hosting and don't even support GitHub Actions yet.

title: Cloud Agents with Subscriptions and Custom Modes
description: Cloud agents gained autonomous capabilities to monitor PRs, watch Slack threads, and run scheduled tasks. New features include custom modes with pinned skills, subagents on isolated VMs, /goal command for persistent objectives, and non-interruptive steering for guiding agents.

title: Grok 4.6 Model Release
description: Cursor released Grok 4.6, a new model focused on long-running agents and complex coding tasks. Features include 500K context window, new XHigh reasoning capability, and improved multi-step reasoning with self-checking. Pricing maintained at $2/$6.

community_feedback.quote: Users reported impressive value overall and strong performance on coding and knowledge tasks.
Some users reported bad experiences with the model not solving problems and high token consumption (>15% usage in a single day).
Issues with auto-overriding without user approval.

title: Cloud Agents 3x Faster Startup with Builds
description: Background preparation of development environments reduces startup time to 3x faster. Agents boot from cached environments with cloned repos and installed dependencies. Failed builds don't disrupt operations as agents continue using last successful build.

title: Google Workspace Plugins
description: New plugins enable agents to work across Gmail (search, draft, send), Google Drive (files, folders), and Google Calendar (events, scheduling). Provides direct integration for workflow automation.

title: Cursor Router with Auto Intelligence
description: Cursor Router optimizes model selection with Auto Intelligence and Auto Balance, delivering 68% lower costs for Intelligence mode while maintaining higher satisfaction.

title: Agent Plugins 1.0 Launch
description: GitHub Copilot launched Agent Plugins 1.0 for VS Code, CLI, and the app, enabling portable agent plugins with multi-catalog search. Features include automatic approval via flags, Cursor skill import and sync, and MCP 2026-07-28 protocol support.

title: Grok 4.6 Model Integration
description: GitHub Copilot integrated Grok 4.6 model, expanding model choices for users. The model is designed for long-running agents and complex coding tasks with improved multi-step reasoning.

title: Code Review Effort Levels GA
description: Code review effort levels became generally available, providing more granular control over automated code review capabilities. Allows teams to customize review depth and automation.

title: Usage Metrics API Expansion
description: Usage metrics API expanded to include agent app activity, providing more detailed insights into how teams are using Copilot across different platforms and workflows.

title: Devin Coach Suggestions
description: Devin introduced real-time prompt improvement suggestions that surface directly in the session input box, helping users formulate better prompts and improve AI interactions.

title: Side Chats Feature
description: Users can now start conversations anchored to any point in a session to ask questions without interrupting Devin's main work flow, enabling parallel exploration and clarification.

title: Automations Queueing Support
description: Automations now support queueing with configurable maximum concurrent runs and queue depth. Users can view queue lifecycle states and manage execution flow more effectively.

title: Security Profiles GA
description: Security profiles became generally available, allowing admins to define profiles governing network access across sessions and automations for improved security control.

title: GitLab Support for Automations
description: Devin Automations now support GitLab triggers and service-account connections, expanding beyond GitHub to support more development workflows.

title: Portable Agent Plugins
description: Codex CLI 0.147.0 introduced Portable Agent Plugins with multi-catalog search, Cursor skill import and sync, and automatic approval via flags. Enhanced secret redaction and improved terminal responsiveness.

title: Linux Desktop App Preview
description: OpenAI Codex released Linux desktop app preview for Ubuntu, Debian, and Fedora distributions. Added import functionality for Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and Cursor configurations.

title: Computer History Feature
description: Computer History launched as an opt-in feature for macOS desktop app, converting app and website activity into memories and timeline data for improved context awareness.

title: Daybreak Cyber Tier Launch
description: Codex introduced Daybreak with two access tiers: 'Daybreak Blue' for general security work and 'Daybreak Red' for specialized cyber operations powered by GPT-5.6 Cyber model.

title: PR Generation and Antigravity Agent
description: Gemini CLI v0.55.1 introduced comprehensive PR generation capabilities with Firestore concurrency dual-locking and the Antigravity agent runner with comprehensive prompt templates.

title: Enhanced Authentication and Security
description: Implemented strict HTTPS validation for GoogleCredentialsAuthProvider to block cleartext leakage, added tag length validation for file keychain system, and improved caretaker triage loop with descriptive comments.

title: Cascade Agent Performance Improvements
description: Windsurf (Codeium) continued performance improvements for the Cascade AI agent, focusing on multi-step autonomous programming capabilities and better context awareness for complex coding tasks.

title: GPT-5 Reasoning Effort Support
description: Aider v0.86.1 added reasoning_effort setting for GPT-5 models and disabled temperature by default for the GPT-5 family, providing more control over advanced model reasoning capabilities.
